{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are invalid and strip token fields",
      "body": "`[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string `'[object Object]'`, not a dynamic key. The second computed key at line 10 also evaluates to `'[object Object]'` and overwrites the first. The resulting zod object only allows `access_token` and a property named `'[object Object]'`, so when credential sharing is enabled it strips `refresh_token`, `expiry_date` / `expires_in`, and all other fields from the sync response. The fallback then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'`. Affected integrations (Google, Office 365, Zoom, Webex, Salesforce) will persist incomplete or corrupt credentials and token refresh will fail."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "External refresh path returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider response objects",
      "body": "In credential-sharing mode this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. Several callers treat the return value as an axios/googleapis style object with `.data` (Google Calendar, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM) or as a token object (HubSpot). With `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set, those code paths access undefined properties and throw or save corrupt credentials. The helper should parse the sync response and return a consistent shape, or all callers must be updated to handle `Response`."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 94,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`token` is undefined when using external credential sync",
      "body": "`const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a fetch `Response` (see refreshOAuthTokens.ts), whose `.data` property does not exist. `token` is undefined and the next line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for self-hosters with credential sync enabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Credential key stores the Zod safeParse result instead of the parsed data",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object `{ success, data }`, not the parsed credential object. Assigning `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then `data: { key }` persists that wrapper as the credential key. Subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the key is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or make the helper return only the parsed data."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`prisma` is used but never imported",
      "body": "The newly added `await prisma.credential.update(...)` uses the `prisma` client, but this file has no `import prisma from '@calcom/prisma';` and no other binding. Constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime. Add the missing import."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Newly refreshed access token is not used for the jsforce connection",
      "body": "The code performs a refresh-token exchange and stores `accessTokenParsed.data` back to the DB, but then creates the connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token`, the old token from the original credential. If that token is expired (the reason a refresh is needed), the connection is built with an invalid token and subsequent Salesforce API calls fail. It should use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`credentialId` is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a user id",
      "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends the third argument as `calcomUserId` to the credential sync endpoint. This call passes `credentialId` (the DB credential record id) instead of `credentialKey.userId` or `credential.userId`. The external platform will receive the wrong user identifier and may sync tokens to the wrong account or reject the request."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Credential find-then-create/update is racy and can create duplicates",
      "body": "The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` without a transaction or uniqueness constraint. If two valid webhook requests for the same user/app arrive concurrently, both can observe no existing credential and both insert a new row. Callers may then pick either credential, leading to split or inconsistent state. Use an upsert based on a unique key or wrap the check/update in a transaction with appropriate locking."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are invalid and strip token fields
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string `'[object Object]'`, not a dynamic key. The second computed key at line 10 also evaluates to `'[object Object]'` and overwrites the first. The resulting zod object only allows `access_token` and a property named `'[object Object]'`, so when credential sharing is enabled it strips `refresh_token`, `expiry_date` / `expires_in`, and all other fields from the sync response. The fallback then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'`. Affected integrations (Google, Office 365, Zoom, Webex, Salesforce) will persist incomplete or corrupt credentials and token refresh will fail.

findings.title: External refresh path returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider response objects
findings.body: In credential-sharing mode this function returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`. Several callers treat the return value as an axios/googleapis style object with `.data` (Google Calendar, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM) or as a token object (HubSpot). With `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` set, those code paths access undefined properties and throw or save corrupt credentials. The helper should parse the sync response and return a consistent shape, or all callers must be updated to handle `Response`.

findings.title: `token` is undefined when using external credential sync
findings.body: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a fetch `Response` (see refreshOAuthTokens.ts), whose `.data` property does not exist. `token` is undefined and the next line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token')`, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for self-hosters with credential sync enabled.

findings.title: Credential key stores the Zod safeParse result instead of the parsed data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object `{ success, data }`, not the parsed credential object. Assigning `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then `data: { key }` persists that wrapper as the credential key. Subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail because the key is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or make the helper return only the parsed data.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: The newly added `await prisma.credential.update(...)` uses the `prisma` client, but this file has no `import prisma from '@calcom/prisma';` and no other binding. Constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime. Add the missing import.

findings.title: Newly refreshed access token is not used for the jsforce connection
findings.body: The code performs a refresh-token exchange and stores `accessTokenParsed.data` back to the DB, but then creates the connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token`, the old token from the original credential. If that token is expired (the reason a refresh is needed), the connection is built with an invalid token and subsequent Salesforce API calls fail. It should use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: `credentialId` is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a user id
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends the third argument as `calcomUserId` to the credential sync endpoint. This call passes `credentialId` (the DB credential record id) instead of `credentialKey.userId` or `credential.userId`. The external platform will receive the wrong user identifier and may sync tokens to the wrong account or reject the request.

findings.title: Credential find-then-create/update is racy and can create duplicates
findings.body: The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` without a transaction or uniqueness constraint. If two valid webhook requests for the same user/app arrive concurrently, both can observe no existing credential and both insert a new row. Callers may then pick either credential, leading to split or inconsistent state. Use an upsert based on a unique key or wrap the check/update in a transaction with appropriate locking.
